# POC results

Status: **all milestones (0–6) implemented.** Everything below was measured on the
**fictional sample corpus** (28 original files, 30 evidence objects) generated by
`src/testing/sample-corpus.ts`. No real legal corpus has been evaluated yet; that is the next
step (see the assessment at the end).

## Milestone 1: ingestion acceptance criteria

Verified by the ingestion tests in `npm test` (86 tests in total), on the synthetic sample
corpus plus 2 deliberately corrupt files and 1 ignored system file.

| Criterion | Result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PDF works | ✅ | Text layer with physical page numbers; headings from font size and numbering |
| Scanned PDF works with OCR | ✅ | Image-only page OCR'd locally (tesseract.js), confidence ~95 on the synthetic scan; chunks flagged `ocr: true` |
| DOCX works | ✅ | Headings → sections, paragraph IDs, lists, tables |
| `.msg` metadata preserved | ✅ | From/To/CC/BCC, subject, sent/received, Message-ID, In-Reply-To, transport headers |
| `.msg` attachments linked to parent | ✅ | By-value attachments and embedded messages (recursive); `attachment_of` relationships |
| `.eml` supported (added) | ✅ | Same schema as `.msg`; MIME attachments and attached messages |
| SHA-256 stored | ✅ | Registry and every canonical record |
| Originals unchanged | ✅ | Manifest before/after on read-only originals: name, size, mtime and SHA-256 identical |
| Duplicate detection | ✅ | Identical copy, email-attachment copy and renamed file all map to one Evidence ID |
| Failures do not stop the batch | ✅ | Corrupt PDF and `.msg` recorded as `failed`; the remaining files ingested |
| No content in the audit log | ✅ | Asserted in the test |

Sample run (synthetic corpus, 4-core cloud VM, OCR on): 28 originals → 30 evidence objects
(5 extracted attachments; 3 byte-identical duplicates detected), about 3.6 s including three
OCR'd scanned pages. The first search after an import also embeds every chunk with the local
model (a few seconds for this corpus; vectors are cached afterwards).

**Caveat: the gold set was used during development.** Failures on it drove fixes; the
history is below. Read the held-out results as the better estimate of behaviour on unseen
questions.

### Held-out set (run once, before further changes)

14 cases written after development (`tests/eval/holdout_cases.yaml`). **First run: 11/14.**

| Case | First run | What went wrong |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H-FACT-004 "When was the administrative inquiry opened?" | ✗ | The answer gave the request's date (17 January 2025) from "…opened into the allegations … in her request of 17 January 2025" instead of the decision's own date. |
| H-CITE-002 "Ms Rossi was interviewed on 24 March 2025" | ✗ **(false VERIFIED)** | 24 March 2025 was Mr Hale's interview, in the next sentence. The verifier's 3-sentence window attributed the date to the wrong person. |
| H-NEG-001 "When was Mr Hale dismissed?" | ✗ | It answered with an unrelated sentence mentioning Mr Hale. "dismissed" never occurs in the corpus. |

Other first-run figures: top-5/top-10 recall 100 %, page correctness 100 %, unsupported claims
0 %, chronology and comparison cases passed.

Fixes (general rules, not case-specific):
- the verifier judges the sentence that matches the claim's subject first;
- question words absent from the corpus need a strong paraphrase;
- performative statements are dated by their document.

After the fixes the held-out set passes 14/14, but that second run is no longer a held-out
measurement.

### Development history on the gold set

| Run | Passed | Main failures found → fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 23/30 | Fabricated quote only downgraded → now UNSUPPORTED. "Ms Doe"/"General Court" counted as evidence → rarity-weighted coverage. Headings returned as answers → typed answers. A comparison pair was missed. |
| 2 | 26/30 | Provenance words ("what document proves") treated as content → ignored. Heading context missing → included. |
| 3 | 28/30 | Comparisons missed paraphrased positions → per-issue aspects, derivational stems. |
| 4 | 29/30 | A corroborating sentence came from another procedure → corroboration must state the same fact. |
| 5+ | 30/30 | Stays 30/30 after the held-out fixes, the date-aware query weights and the score floor. |

### Degraded modes (no downloaded model)

| Semantic provider | Gold cases | Top-5 / top-10 recall | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| local model (default) | 30/30 | 100 % / 100 % | |
| built-in LSA (offline fallback) | 29/30 | 100 % / 100 % | Misses one comparison pair (CMP-002) |
| none (exact words only) | 26/30 | 93.8 % / 93.8 % | Misses 2 chronology events (CHRON-002, CHRON-004) and 3 comparison pairs (CMP-001, CMP-002) |

All targets except the comparison pairs are still met without the model. Semantic search
matters most for comparison and loosely worded chronology questions.

### Comparison quality (manual rating)

The top 6 suggested relations per gold comparison issue (24 pairs) were rated by the
developer (Claude) during development. **They should be re-rated by a legal reviewer.**

| Label produced | Correct | Plausible | Overstated | Wrong |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| potential contradiction (7) | 7 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| possible tension / changed wording (17) | 3 | 4 | 0 | 10 |

The high-severity label is reliable on this corpus. The lower-severity labels are noisy:
typical errors pair sentences from different procedures that share wording (two "registered
on …" sentences) or put a procedural sentence next to a substantive one. Treat them as a
reading list, not findings.

### Verifier behaviour

- **Rejected as intended:** wrong dates, reversed meaning (negation), opposite legal outcomes
  (granted vs rejected), fabricated quotes, non-existent pages and unknown IDs. A quote cited
  from the wrong page is downgraded to PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED with the correct page given.
- **Conservative:** a correct but loosely paraphrased claim can be reported as UNSUPPORTED,
  e.g. "the IAS report did not attribute any shortcoming to any individual" against "the
  findings relate to the design of the process and not to the performance of any individual"
  (17 % word overlap). This is a deliberate trade-off: false negatives over false positives.
- **Not detected:** antonyms outside the legal-outcome list (e.g. "increased" vs
  "decreased") and arithmetic.

## Known limitations

- **Corpus.** Only fictional, synthetic documents (clean PDFs, three synthetic scans) have
  been evaluated. Real scans, long decisions, annex bundles and French/German documents are
  untested.
- **Layout.** pdfjs text order follows the PDF content stream. Multi-column layouts, complex
  tables, headers/footers and footnotes are not reconstructed as Docling would.
- **Headings.** PDF headings are heuristic (font size, numbering, ALL-CAPS lines).
- **OCR** is English-only by default, and typical OCR errors occur (`I` → `|`).
- **Metadata.** Dates, document types and matters are rule-based (`config/*.yaml`) and need
  review and corrections on a real corpus. Matter keywords can over-assign: the Article 24
  request is also tagged `inquiry` and `audit` at low confidence.
- **Search model.** The default model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) is English-only;
  `multilingual-e5-small` is configured but was not tested here (Hugging Face was not
  reachable from the build environment).
- **Hermes.** The MCP server is tested with the official MCP SDK client (stdio and
  in-memory). It has not been tested with a live Hermes installation.
- **Windows launcher.** The `.bat` and `.ps1` were reviewed but not executed (the build
  environment is Linux). The equivalent macOS/Linux launcher was run end to end, including on
  Node 24.
- **Email bodies.** `.msg` files with RTF-only bodies are not decoded.
- **Language.** Language detection is not implemented (`document.language` is `null`).

## Final POC assessment

### What worked

- **Provenance end to end.** Every answer, timeline event, proposition and unaddressed-evidence
  item points to an Evidence ID and a page (PDF) or section/paragraph, and the text can be
  checked mechanically (`chunk.text === unit.text.slice(start, end)`).
- **Immutability.** Originals were unchanged in every test and evaluation run (name, size,
  mtime, SHA-256). Duplicate, renamed and attachment copies map to one Evidence ID.
- **Ingestion breadth.** PDF, scanned PDF (local OCR), DOCX, `.msg` (including embedded
  messages) and `.eml`, with attachments linked to their parent email.
- **Retrieval.** 100 % top-5 recall on both the gold and held-out sets with hybrid search;
  exact references, dates in any format and Article/Annex numbers are reliable.
- **Answers without an LLM.** Extractive answers with typed facts. Refusal works for
  questions the corpus cannot answer, and 0 % of answer claims were unsupported.
- **Citation verification.** It catches deliberately wrong citations: wrong dates, reversed
  meaning, fabricated quotes, wrong pages, missing pages.
- **No-terminal operation.** The double-click launcher, the browser app with every workflow,
  and evaluation from a button.

### What failed or is weak

- **Overfitting risk.** The gold set was also the development set, and the held-out first run
  was 11/14.
- **One false VERIFIED,** found on the held-out set (a date attributed to the wrong person in
  an adjacent sentence). It is fixed, but it shows the verifier needs more adversarial cases.
- **Noisy comparison labels.** Lower-severity relations are about half wrong.
- **Rule-based metadata** over-assigns matters, and document-type rules depend on file naming.
- **Untested here:** a real corpus, the Windows launcher run, live Hermes, multilingual
  documents.

### Accuracy / results (sample corpus)

| | Gold (30) | Held-out first run (14) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Top-10 / top-5 recall | 100 % / 100 % | 100 % / 100 % |
| Citation-support accuracy | 100 % | 80 % |
| Unsupported claims in answers | 0 % | 0 % |
| Refusals | 3/3 | 1/2 |
| Originals unchanged | yes | yes |

### Known risks

- **False VERIFIED results** are the most dangerous failure in a legal setting. The verifier
  is deterministic and conservative, but it was fooled once on unseen data.
- **Synthetic data.** Results come from clean, synthetic documents; real scans and messy
  formatting will lower OCR quality, heading detection and date extraction.
- **Absence detection.** "No treatment found" can be wrong if the decision discusses an
  item in words the system does not link to it. It is always reported as probabilistic.
- **Users may over-trust machine labels.** The UI shows caveats, confidence and the quoted
  source everywhere, but the risk remains.

### What should be built next

1. **Real-corpus evaluation:** 30–50 real files and ≥ 20 real gold questions, plus a fresh
   held-out set, rated by a lawyer.
2. **More adversarial verifier tests:** wrong attribution, partial quotes, numbers and
   amounts, French text. Consider an optional local NLI model as a second opinion
   (never as the only check).
3. **Better layout for real PDFs:** detect running headers/footers, footnotes and tables. If
   real documents need it, consider Docling as an optional parser service.
4. **Multilingual support:** OCR language packs (fra/deu) and the multilingual embedding model,
   tested.
5. **A review workflow in the app:** mark comparison pairs and unaddressed items as
   confirmed/rejected, so ratings are captured, plus a manual-relationship editor (`responds_to`,
   `supersedes`).
6. **Live Hermes integration test** and a Windows launcher test on a clean machine.

### What should NOT be built yet

- **Generative answers as the default.** Keep them optional and verified until the verifier
  has been tested against real data.
- **A graph database.** Relationships fit in JSONL, and no workflow needs graph queries yet.
- **Infrastructure:** RAGFlow/Docker, multiple vector stores, agent frameworks,
  authentication/multi-user features, cloud deployment.
- **Automated legal conclusions** (e.g. "this is a contradiction", "the decision is
  unlawful"). The system should keep producing evidence-linked suggestions for human review.
